projects.title: Karya Indonesia (Karind)
projects.summary: An Indonesian music ecosystem bringing music distribution, merchandise, and concert ticketing together.

coverImage.alt: Karind music platform homepage with music, store, ticketing, studio, and talent navigation
coverImage.caption: Karind homepage: a shared entry point for music, merchandise, ticketing, studio, and talent services.

sections.heading: Overview
paragraphs: Karya Indonesia (Karind) presents an Indonesian music ecosystem in one web platform. Its introduction connects music distribution, merchandise, and concert ticketing, while the main navigation also introduces Studio and Talent services.
The public homepage is the starting point for understanding that wider offer. It needs to communicate the platform’s music identity while giving visitors a clear route into the service they need.

sections.heading: The challenge
paragraphs: A multi-service platform has more than one visitor intent. Someone looking for an event, an artist, or merchandise should not have to interpret the entire ecosystem before choosing where to go.
The interface therefore needs two levels of communication: a concise introduction to Karind as a whole, and distinct entry points for exploring its individual services.

sections.heading: My role & scope
paragraphs: I worked as a full stack programmer, covering frontend and backend development. This case study focuses on the public-facing experience documented in the project preview: the introduction, navigation, search entry point, and account actions.

My typical development range is one to three weeks per project, depending on complexity. The duration above represents that general working range, not a confirmed historical schedule for this release.

sections.heading: Interface approach
paragraphs: The homepage separates its navigation from the main promotional message. Home, Store, Ticketing, Studio, and Talent appear as recognizable destinations, with icons providing an additional visual cue.

A dark foundation keeps the concert photography prominent. Red accents connect the brand mark, selected navigation, registration action, and music-related message, while large white type carries the introduction.

sections.heading: Key features
paragraphs: A prominent search field introduces product, song, event, and artist discovery without requiring visitors to select a service first. Separate Masuk and Daftar actions distinguish returning users from new visitors.

The hero explains the relationship between music distribution, merchandise sales, and concert tickets. Together with the service navigation, it presents the breadth of the platform before visitors continue into a particular area.

sections.heading: Outcome
paragraphs: The homepage brings Karind’s music identity and service entry points into a single public introduction. It communicates a connected platform rather than presenting each service as an unrelated destination.
Search, service navigation, and account access are visible together, allowing the introduction and the next available actions to be read in the same place.

projects.title: Matsuri Castle
projects.summary: A Japanese restaurant landing page with an image-led introduction and an approachable brand experience.

coverImage.alt: Matsuri Castle Japanese restaurant website with sushi photography
coverImage.caption: Matsuri Castle homepage: sushi photography, restaurant identity, and section-based navigation.

sections.heading: Overview
paragraphs: Matsuri Castle is a restaurant landing page built around Japanese food photography and an introduction to the restaurant. It brings promotional content, food highlights, contact information, and a location section into one browsing experience.

sections.heading: The challenge
paragraphs: A restaurant website needs to create an immediate sense of the food while keeping practical information accessible. Large photography can establish the atmosphere, but visitors still need recognizable routes to the menu, restaurant information, and address.

sections.heading: My role & scope
paragraphs: My programming role is full stack development. The work presented here is the static frontend published on GitHub Pages, with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript supported by Bootstrap, jQuery, and Owl Carousel.
The implementation builds on an existing restaurant template, whose original author credit remains in the published source.

sections.heading: Interface approach
paragraphs: The opening composition uses food photography as the main visual, with a high-contrast restaurant message over the image. Section-based navigation provides a way to move beyond the introduction without turning the presentation into a collection of separate pages.

sections.heading: Key features
paragraphs: The published implementation contains an image-led slider, restaurant introduction, food highlights, contact form interface, and address section. Bootstrap styles and a responsive stylesheet provide the layout foundation, while jQuery and Owl Carousel support the presentation interactions.
The food-led introduction is followed by more practical sections, including the contact form interface and restaurant address, giving the page a progression from atmosphere to information.

sections.heading: Outcome
paragraphs: The published page provides a single destination for exploring the restaurant’s visual identity and practical information. Food photography establishes the first impression, while the navigation and supporting sections provide routes into the rest of the presentation.

projects.title: Pasar Iwak
projects.summary: A freshwater fish marketplace connecting buyers, farmers, and sellers, with a focus on the Kendal community.

coverImage.alt: Pasar Iwak freshwater fish marketplace homepage with fish, feed, seed, auction, and seller discovery entry points
coverImage.caption: Original Pasar Iwak homepage: product categories, search, auction promotion, and seller discovery.

sections.heading: Overview
paragraphs: Pasar Iwak is a marketplace for freshwater fish and related products, with an emphasis on the Kendal community. The original homepage brings buyers, fish farmers, and sellers into a shared product-discovery experience.

sections.heading: The challenge
paragraphs: The platform needs to make different types of discovery understandable within the same storefront. Buyers may start with fish, feed, or seed, while others may want to find a seller or explore an auction. Each route needs a recognizable place in the homepage hierarchy.

sections.heading: My role & scope
paragraphs: I contributed as a full stack programmer. This presentation focuses on the marketplace homepage preserved in the project screenshot, including its category navigation, search entry point, account actions, and promotional areas.

sections.heading: Interface approach
paragraphs: The header keeps product navigation, search, the cart indicator, and account actions together. A secondary group of links separates supporting information, marketplace partners, and the community forum from the main shopping navigation.

Below the header, a large fish-farming image introduces the marketplace, while smaller panels give auctions and seller recommendations their own space. Green and teal accents connect the brand identity with the discovery controls.

sections.heading: Key features
paragraphs: The captured interface includes Ikan, Pakan, and Bibit categories, a product search field, Masuk and Daftar actions, a cart indicator, and entry points for Lelang Ikan and Rekomendasi Penjual. Supporting panels also introduce product quality, service, transactions, and contacting sellers.

sections.heading: Outcome
paragraphs: The original homepage brings product discovery and seller discovery into one marketplace introduction. The preserved interface shows how category navigation, search, and promotional routes can coexist without making every visitor follow the same starting path.

projects.title: SIMONE
projects.summary: An online internship registration system for Semarang District Court.

coverImage.alt: SIMONE online internship registration system for Pengadilan Negeri Semarang
coverImage.caption: SIMONE public introduction: online internship registration for Pengadilan Negeri Semarang.

sections.heading: Overview
paragraphs: SIMONE is a web-based internship registration system for Pengadilan Negeri Semarang, or Semarang District Court. Its public introduction explains the service before applicants enter the account-based areas of the system.

sections.heading: The challenge
paragraphs: An institutional application needs to identify the organization and explain its purpose before asking visitors to sign in. The first screen also needs to distinguish learning about the internship service from accessing an existing account.

sections.heading: My role & scope
paragraphs: I worked as a full stack programmer on the web application. The portfolio walkthrough uses the public introduction, rather than applicant records or authenticated screens, to explain the entry experience.

sections.heading: Interface approach
paragraphs: The screen pairs a clear institutional heading and a short service description with an illustration. A green background unifies the page, while white text and controls define the reading order. Login is separated into the header, and Read more provides a second route from the introduction.

sections.heading: Key features
paragraphs: The public page identifies online internship registration as the core service. Its introduction also lists attendance, grades, available places, and certificates as parts of the wider internship experience.
Read more and Login serve different entry needs: understanding the service and accessing an account. Both remain visible without competing with the main institutional message.

sections.heading: Outcome
paragraphs: The public screen gives applicants an identifiable starting point, explains the system’s purpose, and separates information from account access. The introduction communicates the wider internship service without exposing applicant records in the public presentation.

projects.title: SICULI
projects.summary: An internal leave application system for Semarang District Court, bringing leave records and status summaries into an administrative dashboard.

coverImage.alt: SICULI administrative dashboard with leave-status summaries, employee navigation, and a searchable leave-application table
coverImage.caption: SICULI administrative overview: leave-status summaries above the latest application records.

sections.heading: Overview
paragraphs: SICULI is a web-based leave application system for Pengadilan Negeri Semarang. The administrative dashboard brings leave information, organizational data navigation, and application records into one operational view.

sections.heading: The challenge
paragraphs: An administrative user needs both a quick overview and access to individual records. A summary alone cannot explain which request needs attention, while a table alone makes the overall state harder to scan. The dashboard needs to support both levels without mixing them together.

sections.heading: My role & scope
paragraphs: I contributed as a full stack programmer to the web application. This case study focuses on the administrative dashboard shown in the original preview, including its summary cards, record table, and organizational navigation.

sections.heading: Interface approach
paragraphs: A persistent sidebar groups employee and organizational data separately from leave-related records. The main area opens with status summaries before introducing the detailed table of recent applications.
Each summary combines a text label and a count with a color accent. The table then presents the dates, leave type, and status of an application in a consistent row structure.

sections.heading: Key features
paragraphs: The preview distinguishes total, approved, rejected, and postponed leave applications. The application table includes search, a page-size selector, pagination, leave dates, return dates, leave type, and a text status badge.

Sidebar groups provide entry points for employees, supervisors, the chair, employee grades, positions, leave data, and permission data. Keeping these groups in persistent navigation leaves the main content area available for the current operational task.

sections.heading: Outcome
paragraphs: The dashboard places an aggregate view and record-level information on the same screen. Administrators can read the displayed status categories before inspecting individual entries, with search and pagination controls located alongside the detailed records.

faqs.question: What types of projects do you work on?
faqs.answer: I focus on web-based products: portfolio sites, landing pages, dashboards, operational systems, and marketplace-style platforms.

faqs.question: Can you work with an existing design?
faqs.answer: Yes. I can implement an existing design system or help refine the interface direction before development begins.

faqs.question: Do you build both frontend and backend?
faqs.answer: Yes. My work can cover responsive interfaces, backend logic, databases, and API integration depending on the project’s needs.

faqs.question: How do we start a project?
faqs.answer: Start with a short conversation about your goal, users, expected features, and timeline. From there we can define the best next step.

faqs.question: Are you available for collaboration?
faqs.answer: Yes, for selected freelance and collaborative opportunities. Use the contact CTA to get in touch.
